title: Traversable wormholes: shortcuts, negative energy, and what holds them open
question: Can a traversable wormhole carry a payload, or even a signal, between two distant points sooner than light travelling between them through the surrounding space, and can one be held open at all without negative energy? …
bottom_line: No. In established physics no known traversable wormhole delivers a signal, let alone a payload, before light travelling around it, and every throat needs negative null energy: that second part is a theorem of general relativity, and the newer "ordinary matter" designs take their negative energy from the quantum vacuum of ordinary fields. Those designs are real solutions, but deliberately long: the human-scale one takes 9,400 years seen from outside against 0.16 seconds for the traveller. Shortcuts exist only on paper, with hypothetical phantom matter. Nothing passes a kilogram within a century; the cheapest real-universe design needs magnetic monopoles, never observed, and fields 10³⁴ times the laboratory record. The 2022 "wormhole on a chip" tested a teleportation signature, not spacetime. Confidence about 0.9.
